* Port the material model and its store to Dart

Jokes, sets, shows and the library that resolves a set's ids back into
jokes, plus the file store that carries them between launches.

The port's real risk is a value quietly becoming a default, so the
unknown states are what the tests are built around: an unestimated joke
contributes nothing to a set's planned length rather than a guess, an
unknown audience size stays distinct from an empty room across a round
trip, and a descriptor an older build does not recognise decodes to
unknown rather than to the first option of its enum. Confirmed each by
mutation: guessing 60s, and decoding to values.first, both go red.

The store writes aside and renames rather than writing in place. Losing
material to a kill on stage is the one unforgivable bug, and a rename
within a directory is atomic where a partial write is not.

Ids are generated here rather than taken from a package — a v4 UUID is
a few lines, and it is the only thing the product would use one for.

Refs #40

* Port the stage state machine to Dart

The queued/live/told machine behind the card taps, and the segments they
open and close. Tapping a queued card closes the live segment and opens
the next at the same instant, so no gap belongs to neither bit; tapping
the live card is ignored rather than opening a zero-length segment; and
tapping a told card re-opens it while leaving its first segment intact,
which is what the callback in the mockups does.

The started tally counts distinct jokes, not segments, so a bit returned
to still counts once. Mutation-checked, along with the ignored re-tap
and the manual provenance every tap records.

The segment-mode switch throws rather than staying quietly off. A
control that reads "on" while nothing detects would lie on stage.

Refs #40

* Port the review analytics to Dart

The countdown's tone thresholds and the take-anomaly rule.

Both refusals in the anomaly rule are the substance: fewer than three
comparison takes is no norm, and zero spread among them is no signal
rather than an infinitely strong one. Each returns unknown, never a zero
deviation, so a caller cannot mistake "cannot say" for "not anomalous".

The first version of the fewer-than-three test passed for the wrong
reason — its two comparison takes were identical, so the zero-sigma
refusal answered before the count was ever consulted, and lowering the
threshold to two did not red it. It now uses takes with real spread, and
a companion test adds only a third take to pin the boundary.

Refs #40

* Detect laughs from the recording's loudness envelope

The first code in the conversion that is not a port. Decision D7: in a
club, sustained room noise above the room's own level is laughter, and
the product does not need to tell laughter from applause from cheering.
So detection is RMS per frame, a threshold relative to a low quantile of
those frames, and a minimum duration — a pure function of the samples,
with no model, no clock and no I/O, which is what lets requirement 6.9
promise identical events on every platform and every run.

Two choices carry the weight, and both are pinned by a test that fails
when they are reversed:

The baseline is a low quantile, not the mean. On a set that storms,
laughter occupies most of the recording and drags the mean up until the
threshold sits above the laughter itself — the better the set went, the
fewer laughs it would find. Swapping in the mean takes that test from
four events to zero.

Intensity is absolute rather than normalised against the recording's own
peak. Were it relative, every show's best laugh would read 1.0 and takes
from different rooms could not be compared, which is what keeping takes
is for.

The settings live in one named object rather than as defaults spread
through the detector: they are a calibration, and one nobody can point
at is one nobody can review. They are provisional — checked against
synthesised signals only, never against club audio, which is risk R1 and
a Phase B step. The synthetic fixture says so at the point it is built.

* Widen the recording seam and port the capture coordinator

The whole platform surface of the product, and the reason the port is
cheap: with nothing analysing during capture (D8), neither platform has
to hand raw audio to Dart, so what crosses is commands down and small
events up.

The Swift protocol it replaces carried only start, stop, captured and
isRunning — no way for the platform to report a level for the stage
strip, and no way to say the microphone had been taken. Both were
needed, so the seam now carries an event stream: a level to draw, and
interruption transitions. It carries no way to pass samples across at
all, which is requirement 6.7 made structural rather than promised.

The coordinator keeps one file per uninterrupted stretch and a clock
that counts recorded audio rather than wall time, so a stamp indexes

## Preferences

- **End every turn with a blockquote callout** — `> ✅ All done`, or `> ⚠️ Still open: …` listing what remains — never hedged in prose.
- **"LGTM"** merges the change at hand into `main` (`merge-to-main` skill); it approves that change only, never later work.
- **"bump version"** raises the project's version; the project's own workflow decides how it changes and which files change.
- **In the conversation**: link every source-controlled document you edit, display every image you edit, link every issue/PR number.
- **Ask every decision or approval through an `AskUserQuestion` popup, never prose** — one question per item, each with its case.
- **Enclose anything the owner will lift elsewhere** — a prompt, a message, copy to paste — in one delimited block, boundaries unmistakable.
- **Prefix a prompt for another session, inside its block, with a disclaimer**: Claude wrote it — examine inconsistencies, don't follow blindly.
- **Open a pull request right after committing to a branch**, unasked — overriding Claude Code's default of waiting to be told.
- **When handing over a PR to review, describe the folders the change touched in the conversation, in a text box** — a brief line per folder saying what changed there. Show non-test folders only, and ignore README files and comment-only changes.
- **Keep working through a multi-step plan without pausing for approval of each step** — aggregate the steps into one substantial change to review, and stop only for an action that reaches the world (a release, a fleet-wide effect, anything irreversible) or a decision only the owner can make.
- **Never schedule a self check-in to poll a PR** — no recurring wake-up, routine, or `send_later` re-arm that re-reads a PR's state, CI or mergeability on a timer. Act on PR events when they arrive; when nothing has arrived, end the turn.

Four leaves in `dev/requirements/requirements.md` still describe the iPad-only SwiftUI product. Noted during #51 and deferred; this is that work.

**`4.1`** claims "a 3-column grid of nine cards". Since #51 the set list drops to **two** columns below `narrowWidth = 600`, a decision the owner took explicitly (three cards across a phone leaves ~120pt each and clips a title to five characters). The spec never recorded it, so the leaf currently describes behaviour the product does not have on a phone.

**`3.1`** and **`3.4`** say nothing about what the joke panel does when it cannot show everything. Since #51 a narrow *or* short screen caps the panel at `cappedPanelShare = 0.34` of the available height. Under that cap the **body** is what gives — it ellipsizes — while the tags still render, on tightened spacing. That ordering is the decision worth stating: a comedian mid-bit reads the top of the body, and the grid is what they navigate by.

**`5.1`** is a tracked gap whose reason is now **dead**. It reads:

> The standard switch is UIKit-backed, and the renderer behind the screen kind refuses to flatten it — it logs "Unable to render flattened version of PlatformViewRepresentableAdaptor<Switch>"

That is entirely a SwiftUI/UIKit constraint. `stage_screen.dart:429` now uses Flutter's own `Switch`, which Flutter draws itself — there is no platform view to flatten. `StageRegion.segmentMode` already tags it. So this leaf should leave `pending.json` and be claimed by a real screen case, shrinking the burn-down list by one.

Its wording needs care too: it says "a standard **iOS** switch", and the product is now iOS and Android from one codebase.

**`4.1`** claimed a 3-column grid. It drops to two below 600pt of width, because three cards across a phone leaves each about 120pt and clips a title like "Flatmate rota" to five characters.

**`3.1`** and **`3.4`** said nothing about a panel that cannot show everything. A narrow *or* short screen caps it at about a third of the available height — a phone held sideways is wide and still has nowhere to put nine cards. Under the cap the **body** ellipsizes and the tags survive on tighter spacing; that ordering is the claim.

**`5.1`** leaves the burn-down list, so tracked gaps go 14 → 13. Its stated reason was a SwiftUI one — the renderer could not flatten a UIKit-backed control. Flutter draws its own switch, `StageRegion.segmentMode` already tags it, and a screen case now claims it. Its wording drops "iOS": one control on both platforms.

The document's own preamble was stale too, in two places I could not leave while editing around them: it named cases `.case.swift` (the gate enforces `.case.dart`), and carried a banner saying agent sessions have no Swift toolchain so every case runs in CI — the opposite of what the conversion achieved.

requirements  44 passed      sweep exit 0

Two independent defects in the screen kind, found while re-cutting leaves in #78. Both predate that PR. Together they mean the golden gallery — the owner's approval record, and the thing the whole spec-driven method rests on — is much weaker evidence than the document claims.

## 1 — Region crops render the whole screen

`dev/requirements/shared/snapshot.dart` does:

```dart
await expectLater(
  find.byKey(region.key),
  matchesGoldenFile('screen/cases/$slug.$id.png'),
);
```

`matchesGoldenFile` against a `Finder` captures that finder's **nearest ancestor `RepaintBoundary`**, not the widget's own bounds. `stage_screen.dart` contains zero `RepaintBoundary` widgets, so every region walks up to the root and the "crop" is the entire screen.

Measured on `main`:

```
24 screen golden files
 8 distinct images
17 byte-identical           all 834 x 1112, the whole screen
```

So seventeen leaves, each claiming something about a *different element*, are all proved by the same picture. A reviewer approving `2.5`'s countdown colour is looking at the identical bytes as `4.3`'s state key. A change to any one element moves seventeen goldens at once, which reads as the whole kind regressing rather than as one thing changing.

This also silently defeats a convention the document states explicitly and the gate enforces the *declaration* of: "The picture is the smallest surface that proves its leaf… A whole-screen picture is a deliberate exception… and its case says so in a `// whole-screen:` comment the coverage gate demands." Three leaves declare that exception. The other seventeen get whole-screen pictures anyway, without declaring it — the gate checks the declaration, not the resulting image.

**Likely fix:** wrap each tagged region in its own `RepaintBoundary` so it has a layer to capture. Needs care — an extra boundary changes rasterization, so it is a re-baselining event.

## 2 — The requirements harness renders no real glyphs

Every committed golden draws text as filled boxes. `runner_test.dart:17` does call `setUpAll(loadProductFonts)`, but `dev/requirements/pubspec.yaml` has **no `flutter:` section at all**, so none of the fonts bundled in `setlist_ui/pubspec.yaml` reach that package's asset bundle.

The proof is a contrast, not an inference — the same committed assurance test, run in both packages:

```
packages/setlist_ui   test/fonts_render_real_glyphs_test.dart   exit 0   All tests passed
dev/requirements      (same file, copied in)                    exit 1   Test failed
```

That assurance exists precisely to stop this: it renders two strings differing by one character and requires the pixels to differ. It guards the package where the fonts are declared, and not the package that produces every golden in the spec.

The cost is concrete. This spec pins exact copy at more than a dozen leaves — `2.3` **`THE STAND · FRI LATE`**, `2.4` **`8:27 / 20:00`**, `4.3` **`told`/`live`/`queued`**, `4.4` **`SET LIST · 4 / 9`**, `5.1` **`Manual switch`**/**`Autodetect bits`** — and no golden can currently see any of them. Any same-length copy change passes.

## Why this is not fixed in #78

Fixing either one regenerates every screen golden. A committed golden is the owner's approval record, and an agent may propose one for a brand-new leaf but never re-baseline committed ones. Doing both properly is a deliberate refresh whose diff the owner reviews — that is the documented flow for an intended change, and it needs the owner's go-ahead, not an agent's.

Worth doing together rather than separately: each alone rewrites all 24 files, so sequencing them costs two full re-approvals instead of one.

## Suggested order

1. Declare the fonts for `dev/requirements` and **move the assurance test into that package too**, so the gap cannot reopen where it matters.
2. Add the `RepaintBoundary` per region; confirm crops are actually distinct (a cheap check: distinct-image count should approach 24).
3. Refresh all goldens in one pass and review the diff — for most leaves this will be the first time the picture has shown what its line claims.
